newsitem.title: USA: NRC official discloses information illegally.
newsitem.headline: NRC official discloses information illegally.

text.p: A Nuclear Regulatory Commission employee was charged on Friday with illegally disclosing confidential information to a Maine nuclear plant that is under investigation, official said.

Ed Trottier, the NRC's project manager for Maine Yankee, illegally gave plant officials portions of an investigation into the plant's emergency core cooling system, according to the U.S. Attorney's office.

Trottier, 53, of Columbia, Md., was scheduled to appear Friday in U.S. District Court in Portland. Trottier was expected to plead guilty and accept early retirement, NRC and Justice Department officials said.

The 910-megawatt plant in Wiscasset has been under investigation for more than a year over accusations after an anonymous whistleblower alleged plant officials fraudulently manipulated the results of testing on the core cooling system in the 1980s.
The NRC's investigation of the whistleblower's allegations is now being reveiwed by the Justice Department.

The 24-year-old plant has had a series safety-related shutdowns and investigations in the past three years. The NRC recently placed the plant on a Watch List of troubled plants and is considering fines for 16 alleged safety violations.
Maine Yankee is currently off-line to fix misrouted electrical cables and leaking fuel rods and is not expected to return to operation until at least August.

If convicted, Trottier faces a maximum sentence of 1 year n prison and a $100,000 fine, according to the U.S. Attorney's office, which was expected to release more information on the case later Friday.

Maine Yankee is 38 percent owned by Central Maine Power Co, 20 percent each by New England Electric System and Northeast Utilities, seven percent by Bangor Hydro-Electric Co, five percent by Maine Public Service Co, and 10 percent by other New England utilities.
